The recent base rate is around 3.8 to 4.0 percent, with the last six annual prints at 3.8, 3.7, 4.6, 4.2, and 4.0 after December 2025 at 3.8."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanisms: headline level is still near 4 percent; trimmed mean at 3.6 percent argues underlying inflation is sticky; May's -0.7 percent original monthly fall was a downside one-off mostly through volatile categories; July faces administered price and electricity-review seasonality, but July 2025 already had a large 1.3 percent monthly base that should restrain the year-over-year rate. I do not use any catalog point estimate or interval as evidence."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior is May 2026 All groups CPI annual inflation at 4.0 percent, using the Apr-25 to May-26 official complete monthly CPI annual-rate sample. Successive annual-rate changes are -0.3, -0.2, 1.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.2, -0.4, 0.4, 0.0, -0.1, 0.9, -0.4, -0.2, so sigma = 0.48 percentage points. The unadjusted 80 percent half-width is about 1.28*sigma = 0.61 percentage points; I use a 0.7 point half-width because the target is two prints ahead and July energy-policy/base effects matter, but one July 2025 base effect is already known and the annual rate is rounded to one decimal, so widening beyond that would overstate the unresolved shock space. Point update is 4.0 minus 0.2 for the high Jul-25 base partly offset by sticky trimmed mean and housing pressure, giving 3.8 with 80 percent interval 3.1 to 4.5."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk is a large July electricity-price reset or fuel rebound, for example June and July monthly original CPI together exceeding roughly 1.6 percentage points, that keeps the annual rate above 4.5 percent; downside risk is a soft June CPI plus another fuel or recreation decline, for example June and July monthly original CPI together near 0.1 percentage points or lower, that would land below the interval; outside the interval would likely require either a new administered-price shock above the interval or broad monthly deflation below the interval."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: accepted the resolver warning by making the June-vs-July ledger discrepancy explicit and accepted the interval warning by explaining why a 0.7 percentage point half-width is sufficient despite the two-print horizon; also accepted optional clarifications that catalog estimates were not used and made tail scenarios numeric."},{"kind":"forecast","point":3.8,"ciLow":3.1,"ciHigh":4.5}]}
